content.title: About
content.content: Vanilla wafer is a crisp cookie with a delicate vanilla aroma. It is made from a thin dough to which vanilla extract is added, then baked until golden. The wafer works as a standalone snack or as an accompaniment to tea or coffee.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vanilla flavor is obtained from natural vanilla beans or their extract.
Thin layers of dough give the wafer a light, crunchy texture, distinguishing it from denser cookies.
Traditionally popular in Europe, especially in Scandinavian countries and Germany.
Vanilla wafers are often used in dessert compositions as a base for cakes, mousses and ice cream.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Vanilla wafers usually contain a small amount of fat, making them a lighter snack compared with butter-rich cookies.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The dough provides a quick source of energy through simple carbohydrates.

items.title: Vanilla antioxidants
items.content: Vanilla contains antioxidants such as vanillin, which may have mild anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional wafers are made from wheat flour and may be unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Vanilla wafers are often sweetened, so individuals monitoring blood sugar should watch portion size.

items.title: Flavorings
items.content: Some manufacturers use artificial flavorings instead of natural vanilla, which can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie can be enjoyed on its own, broken into pieces and added to ice cream, yogurt or fruit salad. It is also used as a base layer in desserts and cakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the wafer in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent moisture absorption.
